mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts indicates increased demand for housing, which can lead to higher economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of rising housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 0.5% signals an easing monetary cycle, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, which can lead to higher economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of rising payroll employment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, which can lead to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, but only when the unemployment rate is below 6%.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of rising industrial production and low unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures indicates decreased demand, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of declining real personal consumption expenditures (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 2% signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 7% indicates a weak labor market, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, but only when the GDP growth rate is below 2%.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of rising unemployment and low GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production and a decrease in the consumer price index indicates increased economic activity and low inflation, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of rising industrial production and low inflation (t-test p > 0.05).
